objective: Deliver a reviewable, production-candidate AI application that transforms versioned inputs into traceable recommendations through a frozen adapter contract, using only local or existing subscription-backed capabilities, with executable checks and an evidence pack; stop before production deployment or final acceptance.
assumptions: The task brief, acceptance criteria, and adapter contract are frozen and version-controlled before implementation begins.
No paid API calls are permitted; inference, embeddings, evaluation, and development use local models or existing subscription CLIs only.
At most one pilot job may be active at any time.
Repository content, retrieved documents, tool output, and model output are untrusted data.
Secrets, credentials, private source content, and raw Obsidian notes are excluded from commits and evidence artifacts.
PostgreSQL and every required adapter, including pi support if specified by the frozen contract, must be available for a passing pilot; otherwise status remains BLOCKED_ENVIRONMENT.
Any side effect requires an idempotency key, expected revision, and valid fencing token; ambiguous outcomes enter reconciliation and are never blindly retried.
Humans alone authorize permissions, budgets, release acceptance, and production deployment.
architecture: Specification layer: versioned task brief, input/output JSON Schemas, adapter contract, threat assumptions, non-goals, data classification, acceptance thresholds, and explicit human stop conditions.
Ingress layer: schema validation, size and type limits, provenance capture, content sanitization, immutable request identifiers, and rejection of unsupported or sensitive inputs.
Orchestration layer: single-job state machine enforcing CREATED, VALIDATED, RUNNING, RECONCILING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, BLOCKED_ENVIRONMENT, and AWAITING_HUMAN_REVIEW states.

AI layer: provider-neutral model adapter supporting approved local or subscription CLI inference, deterministic configuration where practical, prompt-template versioning, structured outputs, timeouts, and bounded retries for known-safe failures.

Knowledge layer: allowlisted retrieval sources, document-version tracking, chunk provenance, injection-resistant separation of instructions from retrieved data, and citations linking each material claim to its source.
Persistence layer: PostgreSQL-backed job state, append-only audit events, artifact metadata, evaluation results, idempotency records, fencing leases, and migration history.
Side-effect layer: adapter contract requiring validation, dry-run support, idempotency keys, expected revisions, fencing tokens, outcome recording, and reconciliation for unknown results.

Security layer: least-privilege identities, secret injection outside source control, dependency and artifact scanning, output encoding, authorization checks, auditability, retention controls, and fail-closed behavior.

Observability layer: structured redacted logs, traces correlated by job and request identifiers, metrics for quality, latency, failures, resource use, reconciliation, and policy violations, plus actionable alerts.

Release layer: reproducible build, signed or checksummed artifacts, software bill of materials, migration and rollback procedures, evidence pack, reviewer checklist, and a human-controlled release decision gate.

deliveryStages.name: Specification freeze
deliveryStages.outcome: Approve a versioned problem statement, users, use cases, non-goals, data classes, schemas, adapter contract, risk limits, success metrics, and explicit conditions requiring human intervention.
deliveryStages.verification: Schema validation passes; requirement-to-test traceability is complete; contract version is immutable for this pilot; a human reviewer records scope approval without authorizing production.

deliveryStages.name: Environment and dependency readiness
deliveryStages.outcome: Establish a reproducible local development and test environment using only authorized zero-incremental-cost capabilities, with PostgreSQL and all required adapters available.
deliveryStages.verification: Environment preflight reports exact tool and adapter versions; database connectivity and migrations pass; missing pi, PostgreSQL, or contract-required support sets BLOCKED_ENVIRONMENT and prevents pilot success.

deliveryStages.name: Architecture and threat review
deliveryStages.outcome: Document components, trust boundaries, data flows, failure modes, state transitions, side effects, retention, and rollback boundaries.
deliveryStages.verification: Architecture decision records and threat model cover prompt injection, data leakage, authorization bypass, dependency compromise, denial of service, replay, stale writes, and ambiguous side effects; unresolved critical risks block implementation approval.

deliveryStages.name: Test-first implementation
deliveryStages.outcome: Implement the smallest contract-compliant vertical slice: validated ingress, single-job orchestration, AI adapter, persistence, provenance, guarded side effects, and reviewable output.
deliveryStages.verification: Tests first demonstrate required behavior or the prior failure where practical; unit, integration, migration, contract, and failure-path tests pass; npm test exits zero before change proposal.

deliveryStages.name: Evaluation harness and dataset
deliveryStages.outcome: Create a versioned, representative, de-identified evaluation set with expected outcomes, adversarial cases, quality rubrics, and reproducible scoring.
deliveryStages.verification: Dataset provenance and licenses are recorded; leakage and duplication checks pass; baseline and candidate results are reproducible; no private notes, credentials, or production data appear in artifacts.

deliveryStages.name: Quality and safety evaluation
deliveryStages.outcome: Measure task quality, groundedness, schema compliance, abstention, injection resistance, and failure handling against frozen thresholds.
deliveryStages.verification: Automated metrics meet targets; blinded human review samples required outputs; every failure is categorized; critical safety failures are zero; results and raw identifiers are stored in the evidence pack with sensitive content redacted.

deliveryStages.name: Security and privacy hardening
deliveryStages.outcome: Apply least privilege, input validation, authorization, secret management, redaction, dependency controls, retention limits, and secure defaults.
deliveryStages.verification: Static analysis, dependency audit, secret scan, authorization tests, malicious-input tests, and log-redaction checks pass; no high or critical unresolved finding remains.

deliveryStages.name: Observability and operations readiness
deliveryStages.outcome: Provide dashboards, alerts, runbooks, audit trails, service-level indicators, reconciliation procedures, and resource limits for the bounded pilot.
deliveryStages.verification: Synthetic success, failure, timeout, stale-revision, lost-lease, and unknown-outcome scenarios produce expected logs, metrics, traces, alerts, and terminal states without exposing sensitive data.

deliveryStages.name: Rollback and recovery rehearsal
deliveryStages.outcome: Prepare reversible application, prompt, configuration, and database changes with a tested procedure for restoring the last known-good candidate.
deliveryStages.verification: A staging rehearsal restores the prior artifact and compatible database state within the target recovery time; in-flight work is fenced; unknown side effects reconcile; integrity checks pass after recovery.

deliveryStages.name: Release-candidate assembly
deliveryStages.outcome: Produce an immutable candidate containing code, locked dependencies, migrations, configuration schema, model and prompt versions, checksums, SBOM, runbooks, evaluation report, known limitations, and rollback instructions.
deliveryStages.verification: A clean environment reproduces the build and all required checks; artifact checksums match; requirement traceability and evidence-pack indexes are complete; pilot status remains BLOCKED_ENVIRONMENT if any mandatory dependency is absent.

deliveryStages.name: Human release review
deliveryStages.outcome: Submit the candidate and evidence pack for independent human assessment of quality, risk, budget, permissions, operational readiness, and deployment eligibility.
deliveryStages.verification: Named human reviewers record approve, reject, or revise decisions with rationale; absent a recorded human final decision, status remains AWAITING_HUMAN_REVIEW or BLOCKED_ENVIRONMENT; no automated process deploys or marks the pilot accepted.

metrics.name: Requirement coverage
metrics.target: 100% of frozen functional, safety, and operational requirements map to at least one executable check and evidence artifact.
metrics.measurement: Generate a traceability matrix and fail the release check for any unmapped or failing requirement.

metrics.name: Structured-output validity
metrics.target: At least 99.5% valid outputs on the evaluation set and 100% fail-closed handling of invalid outputs.
metrics.measurement: Validate every response against the versioned output JSON Schema and record validation and recovery outcomes.

metrics.name: Grounded claim rate
metrics.target: At least 95% of material factual claims are supported by retrieved, versioned evidence; unsupported high-impact claims are zero.
metrics.measurement: Use automated citation checks followed by blinded human review of a statistically defined sample.

metrics.name: Task quality
metrics.target: At least 90% rubric pass rate and no regression greater than 2 percentage points versus the approved baseline.
metrics.measurement: Run the frozen evaluation dataset with deterministic settings where practical and apply a blinded human rubric to sampled results.

metrics.name: Safety and injection resistance
metrics.target: 100% of critical adversarial cases are blocked, safely handled, or explicitly abstained; zero secret or private-content disclosure.
metrics.measurement: Execute the versioned adversarial suite covering prompt injection, exfiltration, unsafe tool requests, malformed inputs, and authorization bypass.

metrics.name: Reliability
metrics.target: At least 99% successful completion for valid evaluation jobs, excluding declared environment blockers.
metrics.measurement: Run repeated integration scenarios and calculate success by terminal state with failures categorized.

metrics.name: Single-job enforcement
metrics.target: Zero instances of more than one active pilot job.
metrics.measurement: Concurrent-start tests query persisted leases and state transitions and verify all extra starts are rejected or queued.

metrics.name: Side-effect integrity
metrics.target: 100% of side-effect attempts carry idempotency key, expected revision, and valid fencing token; zero blind retries after unknown outcomes.
metrics.measurement: Inspect adapter contract-test traces and persisted audit events for required fields and reconciliation transitions.

metrics.name: Latency
metrics.target: Candidate-specific p95 end-to-end latency is no worse than the frozen release threshold measured on the approved reference hardware.
metrics.measurement: Record warm and cold latency histograms under a documented, reproducible workload without paid services.

metrics.name: Observability coverage
metrics.target: 100% of defined critical state transitions and failure modes emit correlated, redacted telemetry and actionable alerts.
metrics.measurement: Inject each documented scenario and verify expected log, metric, trace, and alert evidence by request and job identifier.

metrics.name: Security findings
metrics.target: Zero unresolved critical or high findings and zero committed secrets.
metrics.measurement: Run static analysis, dependency audit, secret scanning, authorization tests, and manual threat-model review; archive reports.

metrics.name: Rollback readiness
metrics.target: Restore the last known-good candidate within 15 minutes with no audit-log loss and verified database compatibility.
metrics.measurement: Time a staging rollback rehearsal and compare artifact, schema, state, and audit integrity before and after recovery.

metrics.name: Reproducibility
metrics.target: Two clean runs from locked inputs produce equivalent artifacts and metric results within documented deterministic tolerances.
metrics.measurement: Rebuild and reevaluate in clean environments, compare checksums where deterministic, and document permitted model variance.

risks.risk: Required PostgreSQL, pi support, local model, or adapter capability is unavailable.
risks.mitigation: Fail preflight, preserve BLOCKED_ENVIRONMENT, prohibit simulation of success, and escalate the exact missing capability to a human.

risks.risk: Prompt injection or untrusted retrieved content changes application behavior.
risks.mitigation: Separate system instructions from data, allowlist sources, sanitize content, restrict tools, validate outputs, test adversarial inputs, and require human review for high-impact actions.

risks.risk: Sensitive data or secrets leak into prompts, logs, artifacts, or commits.
risks.mitigation: Classify and minimize data, redact telemetry, inject secrets at runtime, scan commits and artifacts, block raw private notes, and enforce retention limits.

risks.risk: Model output is inaccurate, unsupported, or inconsistent.
risks.mitigation: Require source provenance, structured validation, calibrated abstention, frozen evaluation thresholds, human sampling, and explicit uncertainty in user-visible results.

risks.risk: Duplicate, stale, or split-brain side effects occur.
risks.mitigation: Require idempotency keys, expected revisions, transactional state changes, single-job leases, fencing tokens, and reconciliation of ambiguous outcomes.

risks.risk: Dependency or build compromise affects the candidate.
risks.mitigation: Lock dependencies, generate an SBOM, scan vulnerabilities, verify checksums, restrict registries, and reproduce builds in a clean environment.

risks.risk: Zero paid API budget is accidentally exceeded.
risks.mitigation: Disable paid providers and network credentials by default, maintain an allowlist of local or existing subscription CLIs, and expose usage and cost counters with a hard zero-paid-call policy.

risks.risk: Evaluation data is unrepresentative, contaminated, or leaked into development.
risks.mitigation: Version dataset provenance, separate development and holdout sets, check duplicates, use blinded review, and document known coverage gaps.

risks.risk: Telemetry is insufficient to diagnose incidents or contains sensitive content.
risks.mitigation: Define required events before implementation, correlate telemetry, test redaction and alerts, retain append-only audit metadata, and rehearse incident scenarios.

risks.risk: Rollback fails because code, prompts, configuration, model, and schema versions diverge.
risks.mitigation: Bundle compatible versions, use backward-compatible migrations where possible, retain the last known-good artifact, fence in-flight jobs, and rehearse rollback before review.

risks.risk: Automation implicitly treats passing checks as authorization to deploy or accept the pilot.
risks.mitigation: Keep technical readiness separate from governance decisions, require recorded human approval, prevent deployment credentials from being available to the implementer, and leave productionDeploymentAuthorized and finalApprovalClaimed false.
